summary: Luigi Pio Tessitori was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Florence under Paolo Emilio Pavolini from circa 1906 to 1910.

Luigi Suali worked in Indology and philosophy, studying under Francesco Lorenzo Pullè at the University of Bologna and Hermann Jacobi at Bonn. He held posts at Bologna and later at the University of Pavia as professor (1909–1910, 1914–1956).

Luigia Nitti-Dolci specialized in Indology and linguistics. She earned her Dr.-ès-lettres at the University of Paris studying under Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, and Theodor Bloch, and served as editor of Nepalese manuscripts at the Institut de Civilisation Indienne.

An Indologist, Luis González-Reimann studied at UNAM, El Colegio de México, and UC Berkeley under Robert P. Goldman. He lectured at various Mexican universities and held a post as lecturer and research scholar at UC Berkeley (attested 1996–2014).

Luis Oscar Gómez worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning degrees from the University of Puerto Rico, Yale under Stanley Insler, and the University of Michigan. He served as professor and department chair at the University of Michigan.

Luise Hercus specialized in Indology and linguistics, studying at St Anne's College and the Australian National University. She held posts at St Anne's College (1948–1954), the University of Adelaide (1965–1969), and the Australian National University (circa 1969–1991).
Luise Hilgenberg was an Indologist who completed a Dr.med. and a Dr. phil. at the University of Bonn, studying for the latter under Willibald Kirfel circa 1928–1933.

Lumír Jisl worked in archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, graduating from Charles University in 1949. He held posts at the Institute of Archaeology of the CAS in Prague (1956) and Charles University (1960).
Lungten Dubgyur works in Tibetology and other fields. He earned degrees from Sherubtse College, Government Law College, Mumbai, and the University of Edinburgh.

Lungtok Tenpai Nyima worked in Tibetology and religious studies, earning a Geshe degree at Kyangtsang Monastery under Tendzin Lodro Gyatso. He founded Menri Monastery and served as its abbot beginning in 1969.
Lungtok Tenpé Nyima studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.
Sinologist Lutz Bieg completed his Dr. phil. at Heidelberg University and his Habilitation at Freie Universität Berlin. He served as ordinary professor at the University of Cologne from 1989 to 2008.

Working in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, Lyne Bansat-Boudon studied under Armand Minard and doctoral supervisor Marie-Claude Porcher. She held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the Institut Universitaire de France.

Lynette Monteiro works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her Ph.D. at the University of Ottawa and held posts at Sea Glass Psychological Services (1997) and the Ottawa Mindfulness Clinic (2003).
Lynken Ghose is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who held posts at McGill University (attested 1998–2000) and Iowa State University (attested 2000).

Lynn Struve specializes in sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Washington and the University of Michigan, and held a post at Indiana University Bloomington from circa 1977 to 2011.

Lynn Teskey Denton was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at McMaster University and Somerville College. She taught at McMaster University and served as Assistant Professor at Concordia University from 1984 to 1989.

Lynn Thomas works in Indology and religious studies, having studied at Lancaster University and the University of Oxford. Thomas held a post as lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton (attested 1997).

László Gaál worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. Educated at Franz Joseph University and Göttingen under multiple scholars, he held posts at Eötvös Loránd University (1948–1958) and the University of Debrecen (1957).

Léon Feer worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, studying under Foucaux, Pavie, Mohl, and Quatremère. He held posts at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, Collège de France, EPHE, and the Bibliothèque nationale de France.
